evals.name: rename-db-column-expand-contract
evals.prompt: /small-safe-steps Rename the 'email' column to 'email_address' in the users table
evals.expected_output: Should detect this is a risky DB change and apply expand-contract pattern. Must include dual-write phase, migration phase, and cleanup phase with a waiting period before dropping the old column.

assertions.text: Identifies this as a risky breaking change that cannot be done in one step
Proposes at least 3 phases following expand-contract: Expand (add new column + dual-write), Migrate (switch reads), Contract (drop old column)
Expand phase includes dual-write — writing to BOTH old 'email' and new 'email_address' columns simultaneously
Contract phase explicitly requires verifying zero usage of old column for days/weeks before dropping it — does NOT drop immediately
Each individual step is scoped to 1-3 hours maximum — no step is described as taking a full day or more
Does NOT propose renaming the column in a single step (ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN as the only step)
Reads the fixture project's user_service.py to reference real column names and code before planning

evals.name: add-caching-no-expand-contract
evals.prompt: /small-safe-steps Add an in-memory cache to the get_user method so repeated lookups don't hit the database
evals.expected_output: Should NOT apply expand-contract (this is an additive change with no breaking risk). Should break into simple phases: add cache → test → deploy. Each step 1-3h.

assertions.text: Does NOT apply expand-contract pattern — recognizes this is an additive, non-breaking change
Proposes phases appropriate to the risk: add cache implementation, add tests, deploy — no elaborate dual-write or migration phases
Each individual step is scoped to 1-3 hours maximum
Notes that adding a cache is reversible (can be removed without data loss) and therefore low-risk
Reads user_service.py to understand the actual get_user implementation before planning

evals.name: replace-email-service-expand-contract
evals.prompt: /small-safe-steps Migrate our email sending from SendGrid to AWS SES
evals.expected_output: Should apply expand-contract for service replacement. Expand phase adds SES alongside SendGrid. Migrate phase routes traffic gradually. Contract phase removes SendGrid only after zero usage verified.

assertions.text: Identifies this as a service replacement — a risky change that needs expand-contract
Expand phase includes sending via BOTH SendGrid and SES simultaneously (dual-send) before switching
Migrate phase proposes gradual traffic routing (feature flag, percentage rollout, or canary) rather than a hard cutover
Includes an explicit monitoring/verification step after routing traffic to new service before removing old one
Contract phase removes SendGrid only after confirming zero usage — not immediately after 100% routing
Includes a learning step (time-boxed investigation) to understand current SendGrid usage before building anything
Each individual step is scoped to 1-3 hours maximum

evals.name: resist-pressure-quick-api-rename
evals.prompt: /small-safe-steps Rename the 'userName' field to 'username' in the public REST API response. It's just a field rename, shouldn't take long.
evals.expected_output: Should resist the user's minimization ('shouldn't take long') and apply expand-contract. Must explain that API consumers will break if old field disappears suddenly. Deprecation period required.

assertions.text: Identifies this as a breaking API change that will affect external consumers — even though user says 'it's quick'
Does NOT agree with the user's framing that 'it shouldn't take long' — explains why it needs a careful approach
Expand phase includes returning BOTH 'userName' and 'username' fields simultaneously so existing consumers don't break
Includes an explicit deprecation period before removing 'userName' — not an immediate removal after adding 'username'
Mentions notifying API consumers or adding deprecation headers/warnings before removing the old field
Each individual step is scoped to 1-3 hours maximum

evals.name: string-to-json-data-migration
evals.prompt: /small-safe-steps Migrate the event_log.metadata column from storing plain strings to storing structured JSON objects
evals.expected_output: Should detect this is a data type + format change requiring backfill of existing rows. Expand-contract with: add new column, dual-write, backfill existing rows, switch reads, drop old. Must time-box the backfill as a separate learning step.

assertions.text: Identifies this needs backfilling of existing rows in the database — not just changing new writes
Expand phase adds a new 'metadata_json' column (or similar) alongside the existing 'metadata' string column
Backfilling existing rows is a separate step from adding the new column — not bundled together
Backfill step is time-boxed or batched (not a single bulk UPDATE of all rows at once) to avoid locking the table
Dual-write (writing to both columns) remains active throughout the entire migration phase until reads are fully switched
Reads the fixture project's event_log.py to understand the actual schema and code before planning
Each individual step is scoped to 1-3 hours maximum
Includes a learning step to understand the current data distribution (e.g., how many rows, what formats exist) before starting any migration

evals.name: microservice-extraction
evals.prompt: /small-safe-steps Extract the payment processing logic from the order_service into a separate PaymentService microservice
evals.expected_output: Should break extraction into multiple phases: characterize current behavior, build new service alongside, route traffic incrementally, decommission old code. Must identify this as a high-risk multi-week effort requiring careful incremental steps.

assertions.text: Identifies this as a high-risk, multi-week effort — not a task that can be done in a single sprint
First phase is characterization/learning: understand current payment logic behavior, write tests that capture it, time-boxed
New PaymentService is built alongside the existing code (expand), not as a replacement from the start
Includes a migration phase with gradual traffic routing (dual-call or feature flag) before decommissioning old code
Reads order_service.py to reference actual method names and logic before planning
Explicitly separates learning steps (investigation, characterization, spike) from earning steps (ship working service)
Each individual step is scoped to 1-3 hours maximum
Does NOT propose a big-bang cutover — does NOT say 'move all payment code to new service and update all callers in one step'

evals.name: trivial-task-no-overengineering
evals.prompt: /small-safe-steps Fix the typo in the error message on line 42 of user_service.py where 'recieved' should be 'received'
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this is too small for a multi-phase plan. Should suggest doing it directly rather than creating an elaborate step breakdown. Must NOT apply expand-contract or create phases for a one-line fix.

assertions.text: Recognizes the task is trivial (< 1 hour) and does not require a multi-phase plan
Does NOT apply expand-contract pattern or create multiple phases for a one-line text change
Suggests doing the fix directly rather than planning it out as a structured multi-step effort
Does NOT produce a step plan with phases like 'Phase 1: Identify typo', 'Phase 2: Fix typo', 'Phase 3: Verify fix'

grading_guide.capability_assertions: The output demonstrates the stated reasoning or produces the stated content. Evidence must be explicit in the response, not inferred.
grading_guide.behavior_assertions: The output does or avoids the described action. Binary: did it happen or not.
grading_guide.statistical_requirements: With min_runs=3, report mean, stddev, min, max per metric. A delta is only meaningful if confidence intervals don't overlap.
